_note: Connection timeouts in milliseconds, read by the server and the client at start (a server restart is needed for a change). A game that freezes for a while (loading, a slow machine) is not dropped until max passes with no answer.
_note_packet_throttle: ENet's packet throttle (Dave 23 Nov 2026, first game on the real server: animals "teleporting and jumping right through us"; docs/design/ANIMAL_NETCODE.md). Each time a ping comes back slower than the recent ones, ENet lowers a share and then drops that share of the unreliable packets on purpose before they are sent (ENet peer.c enet_peer_throttle, protocol.c). Over the internet the ping wobbles all the time, so it threw away animal rows, other players' positions and our own position reports; on a LAN it never wobbles, so tests never saw it. Deceleration 0: the share never falls, nothing is dropped on purpose (the ENet defaults are 5000, 2, 2). Our unreliable traffic is a few kB a second; a real loss is still a loss.
_note_block_line: The direct block line (block_link_server.gd): blocks a player's game has not taken yet wait in an outbox of at most block_line_outbox_kb; while it is full, further blocks go over the game connection. A line that takes nothing for block_line_stall_ms while blocks wait is dropped, and that player gets blocks over the game connection. One player who stops reading never holds the block workers for everyone.
_note_block_line_hello: A new block line has block_line_hello_ms to say which player it is (the game sends it from its own frame, which on a cold first join comes after a 5-6 s freeze); at most block_line_pending_max connections wait at once.
